assessments.reasoning: Section 3.2.2.1 ties the opposite-sign nonexact quotient choice to the implementation and explains floored and symmetric directions. The two tables give different quotients for opposite-sign operands. The scope is the default choice, and the draft directs dependent programs to specify division explicitly or state an environmental dependency.

challenge.method: Compared signed versus unsigned, same-sign and opposite-sign examples, and default behavior versus the separately specified FM/MOD entry on PDF page 61.
challenge.results: The draft's default is implementation-defined for the stated nonexact signed case. Explicit floored FM/MOD provides a direct counterexample to a claim that every division word delegates rounding.

limitations: This does not change Core words whose entries specify their own rounding behavior or assert a particular system default.
